nodes.title: Normal inertia subgroups
nodes.statement: For an algebraic stack X locally of finite presentation over S, a rigidifiable inertia subgroup is a closed subgroup G⊂I_X that is flat and finitely presented over X. For every T→X represented by x, it yields G_x⊂Aut_T(x); every base change identifies the pulled-back subgroup, and every isomorphism x≅y conjugates G_x onto G_y. In particular G_x is normal; centrality is not required. The site-level carrier records normal subgroups of native Aut groups, conjugation, restriction and fppf local membership, with the closed/flat/finitely-presented representability conditions imposed at the algebraic-stack interface.
hypotheses: X is algebraic and locally of finite presentation over S.
G is a representable closed subgroup of inertia, flat and finitely presented over X.
proofSteps: Use SF.1/inertia to identify the stabilizer over each object.
Pull back the subgroup along every test-scheme arrow, including isomorphisms; compatibility under automorphisms implies normality.
Membership is local for the fppf topology because G is a subgroup sheaf; retain this locality in the native pseudofunctor interface.
acceptance: Accept varying subgroup schemes and noncentral normal subgroups.
A finite relative inertia kernel is not automatically flat; it can be used here only after flatness and finite presentation are checked.

sources.locator: Appendix A, setup before Theorem A.1, pp.1086–1087
sources.match: A closed flat finitely presented inertia subgroup gives compatible closed subgroup families; isomorphism compatibility forces normality.
For a group algebraic space the identity is closed exactly when the group is separated. Apply this on inertia charts to the geometric bottom constructor.
A1_k/Z is a non-separated finite-type group algebraic space. Its classifying stack supplies the counterexample to unconditional geometric bottom.

nodes.title: Rigidification of an algebraic stack
nodes.statement: Given X and a rigidifiable G⊂I_X, construct X▹G by replacing the Isom sheaf between x and y over T by its fppf quotient Isom_X(x,y)/G_x, where G_x acts by precomposition, and then stackifying the resulting prestack. Normality identifies the right and left actions and makes composition well defined. The map ρ:X→X▹G has the same locally presented objects and kills precisely G. X▹G is an algebraic stack locally of finite presentation over S. The sheaf quotient is essential: its T-sections need not equal the quotient of the T-section sets.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of normal-inertia-subgroup.
All Hom quotients are taken as fppf sheaves before object descent.
proofSteps: Define the normal Hom congruence using precomposition, with coherence under every restriction. Use native CategoryTheory.Quotient only for its fibrewise precursor.
The free G_x-action on the Isom algebraic space has an algebraic-space fppf quotient; use SF.1 categorical quotient descent.
Sheafify quotient morphisms, then use SF.1/stackification for effective object descent.
An fppf local lift identifies a fibre with BG_x. Algebraicity follows from SF.1/algebraic-stack and the gerbe atlas; smoothness of the gerbe is treated below.
acceptance: Do not replace the stack by an orbit set.
The quotient on global sections is asserted only for point-site fixtures, never for an arbitrary test scheme.

sources.match: Quotient Isom sheaves are composed and stackified; the resulting algebraic stack has the prescribed stabilizer kernel.

nodes.title: Universal property of rigidification
nodes.statement: For every stack Y in groupoids over S, precomposition with ρ induces an equivalence of Hom groupoids Hom_S(X▹G,Y) ≃ Hom_S(X,Y)_{G=1}, where the right side is the full subgroupoid of morphisms whose induced automorphism maps kill G on every test object. Thus such a morphism has a factorization together with a comparison 2-isomorphism; the groupoid of factorizations with that fixed comparison is contractible. This is a statement about morphisms and compatible 2-morphisms, not equality of chosen factors.
hypotheses: X,G,ρ as in rigidification.
Y satisfies stack descent; algebraicity of Y is unnecessary.
proofSteps: A G-killing functor factors on every quotient Hom sheaf; its restriction coherence descends.
Apply stackification universality to extend to objects and morphisms of X▹G.
Modifications descend because they satisfy the same Hom-sheaf compatibility. Full faithfulness gives uniqueness relative to the supplied comparison.
acceptance: Retain nontrivial automorphisms of factors and comparison 2-isomorphisms.
A target algebraic space is one special case, not the universal target class.

sources.match: Universal factorization for a compatible fixed subgroup; the general varying subgroup is supplied by AOV.

sources.locator: Appendix A quotient-Hom construction and Remark A.2, pp.1087–1089
sources.match: The construction and uniqueness imply the full stack-valued universal property when combined with stackification.

nodes.title: Stabilizers after rigidification
nodes.statement: For x∈X(T), the map Aut_T(x)→Aut_T(ρx) is an epimorphism of fppf group sheaves with kernel G_x; consequently Aut_T(ρx)≅Aut_T(x)/G_x as fppf sheaves. This need not be a surjection on T-valued automorphisms.
hypotheses: X,G,ρ as in rigidification.
proofSteps: Specialize the quotient-Hom formula to x=y.
Identify the identity fibre with G_x by the normal congruence.
The quotient-sheaf construction gives local surjectivity; multiplication is inherited from composition.
acceptance: BC4/C2 has residual stabilizer C2.
The G_m/μ_2 example prevents a global-section surjectivity claim.

sources.match: Stabilizer map is surjective as a sheaf with the chosen kernel.

nodes.title: Geometry of the rigidification morphism
nodes.statement: ρ is an fppf gerbe, smooth and of finite presentation as a morphism of algebraic stacks. It is proper when G→X is finite, and étale when G→X is étale. If X is Deligne–Mumford, then X▹G is Deligne–Mumford and ρ is étale. Smoothness of ρ does not say that G is smooth or that ρ is representable. When G is nontrivial, ρ is not representable.
hypotheses: X,G,ρ as in rigidification.
The proper and étale assertions have the extra subgroup hypotheses stated.
proofSteps: After an fppf local lift y=ρx, identify X×_{X▹G}T with BG_x, as in AOV pp.1088–1089.
Apply the classifying-stack geometry supplied by SF.1; B of a flat finitely presented group is smooth as a stack even if its torsor atlas is merely flat.
For finite G use finite diagonal and universal closedness of the gerbe to get properness. For étale G use étale stack charts.
For a DM source its flat finitely presented inertia subgroup is unramified and hence étale; the quotient Isom spaces remain unramified.
acceptance: Bμ_p→Spec(k) is a smooth stack morphism in characteristic p.
BC2→Spec(k) is an étale gerbe with nontrivial inertia, not a representable finite étale morphism.

sources.locator: Theorem A.1(a) and final paragraph, pp.1087–1089
sources.match: Gerbe description and local BG model give smoothness; finite and étale subgroup cases give proper and étale maps.

The fixed-subgroup case preserves DM stacks and descends separatedness/properness of the source stack to the rigidified stack. Properness of the rigidification map for finite G is supplied by AOV Theorem A.1.

nodes.title: Base change of rigidification
nodes.statement: For any morphism S′→S, (X×_S S′)▹(G×_S S′)≃(X▹G)×_S S′, compatibly with ρ and quotient Hom sheaves. More generally, pulling the gerbe ρ back along T→X▹G gives the rigidification by the pulled-back subgroup. No flatness or tameness assumption on S′→S is needed.
hypotheses: X,G,ρ as in rigidification.
The subgroup is pulled back with the stack, not held fixed as a group of global sections.
proofSteps: Flatness and finite presentation of the subgroup survive arbitrary base change.
Compare quotient Hom sheaves and use effective stack descent; alternatively use the universal property on the base-changed gerbe.
The comparison respects the map from X and is unique relative to it.
acceptance: Specialize to a nonreduced base extension.
Keep this assertion distinct from the flat-only base-change theorem for a general coarse space.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.1, last assertion before the proof, p.224
sources.match: Fixed-subgroup rigidification commutes with base change.
The subgroup-family and quotient-sheaf construction gives the varying-subgroup comparison.

nodes.title: Nested rigidifications
nodes.statement: Suppose H⊂G⊂I_X are compatible closed normal subgroup stacks flat and finitely presented over X, and the descended quotient G/H on X▹H is also closed, flat and finitely presented. Then (X▹H)▹(G/H)≃X▹G, compatibly with the maps from X. On stabilizers the composite removes exactly G; the order of removal is governed by H⊂G and cannot be interchanged for arbitrary unrelated subgroups.
hypotheses: Both rigidifications are defined with the listed geometric subgroup conditions.
proofSteps: Use the first quotient-Hom formula to identify the residual subgroup G/H.
A stack morphism from X kills G iff it factors through X▹H and kills G/H.
Apply the universal property twice, including the factor comparison 2-isomorphisms.
acceptance: For C8 with subgroups C2⊂C4, two successive quotients give BC2, matching BC8▹C4.

sources.locator: Appendix A construction and Remark A.2, pp.1087–1089
sources.match: Successive normal Hom quotients and uniqueness yield this formal consequence; it is not separately numbered in the source.

nodes.title: Coarse spaces are preserved by rigidification
nodes.statement: X admits a coarse moduli space π:X→M iff X▹G does; the same M works, and π factors through ρ. The two coarse morphisms have the same universal algebraic-space targets and geometric isomorphism classes. This does not make X▹G fine: it can retain stabilizers and nontrivial forms.
hypotheses: X,G,ρ as in rigidification.
Coarse moduli space means the SF.1 definition, universal among all algebraic spaces.
proofSteps: Every map to an algebraic space kills all automorphisms, so the universal property identifies the categories of such maps.

Over an algebraically closed field, an fppf gerbe with a flat finitely presented band has a local lift and a rational point on a nonempty finite-type local cover; its objects form one isomorphism class over each image.
Combine categorical universality and the geometric-point bijection.
acceptance: BC4▹C2 still has coarse Spec(k) and residual C2.
A common coarse space supplies no universal elliptic family.

sources.match: The original and rigidified stacks have the same coarse moduli space.

sources.locator: Theorem A.1 and Remark A.2, pp.1087–1089
sources.match: The gerbe and universality extend the same conclusion to varying normal subgroup stacks.

nodes.title: Rigidification by vertical inertia
nodes.statement: For a morphism f:X→Y of algebraic stacks, let G=I_{X/Y}=ker(I_X→f*I_Y). If this kernel is a closed subgroup flat and finitely presented over X, there is a factorization X→X▹G→Y with a comparison 2-isomorphism, and the final map is representable by algebraic spaces. The rigidification has the universal property of killing the vertical inertia. No such factorization by this construction is asserted when the relative inertia is not flat.
hypotheses: X is locally of finite presentation over S.
G=I_{X/Y} has the stated closedness, flatness and finite-presentation conditions.
Y is algebraic.
proofSteps: Kernel normality and base-change compatibility put G in normal-inertia-subgroup.
f kills G, hence factors by the universal property.

On the quotient stabilizer sheaves the remaining map is injective on every test scheme. Its base change to any scheme over Y is an algebraic stack with trivial inertia, hence an algebraic space by SF.1/setoid-criterion. This proves the representability definition; geometric-point injectivity alone is insufficient.
acceptance: For BC4→BC2 induced by the quotient, the final factor is BC2→BC2.
For a monomorphism of groups, the kernel is trivial and the original classifying-stack map is representable.
Finite inertia alone is insufficient to justify flatness of G.

sources.match: The subgroup quotient has exactly the specified stabilizer kernel.
Representability is equivalent to trivial relative inertia, using automorphism sheaves on all test schemes.

nodes.title: Recovery of affine-kernel gerbe rigidification
nodes.statement: For a morphism of affine fpqc gerbes over a field, when its stabilizer kernel is flat and finitely presented so that the general construction applies, the intermediate affine gerbe of R09.5/affine-kernel-rigidification is equivalent to X▹G, with the same factorization and quotient Isom sheaves. nodes.title: Auxiliary levels and stabilizer quotients
nodes.statement: A representable auxiliary-level morphism p:L→X identifies Aut(ℓ) with the stabilizer subgroup of Aut(pℓ) preserving the chosen level. It removes automorphisms by taking a subgroup and changes the objects; rigidification X→X▹G keeps locally lifted objects and takes the quotient Aut(x)/G_x. These operations coincide only after an additional comparison is proved. A rigidifier with trivial level-preserving automorphisms gives an algebraic-space moduli object if its full sheaf-valued inertia is trivial, but a coarse space merely records geometric isomorphism classes. Concrete elliptic rigidifiers are imported from ModularCurves4C; abelian and PEL levels remain downstream consumers.
hypotheses: p is representable; all automorphism assertions are about sheaves.
To infer an algebraic space, trivial inertia is proved on all test schemes.

nodes.title: Finite correspondences over a base
nodes.statement: For separated Deligne–Mumford stacks X,Y of finite type over a locally Noetherian S and with finite inertia, a finite correspondence is a span X←p Z→q Y over S, with both p and q representable by algebraic spaces and finite. Morphisms are equivalences of the middle stacks with compatible 2-isomorphisms on both legs. The correspondence is not defined as its image in X×_S Y: the middle stack and its multiplicities are retained. Since Y is separated over S, the joint map Z→X×_S Y is finite: factor through the graph over X and use the proper quasi-finite diagonal of Y. This supplies a finite-algebra presentation for descent.
hypotheses: X,Y are separated finite-type DM stacks over locally Noetherian S, with finite inertia.
Both legs, not just one, are representable and finite.
proofSteps: Use SF.1/two-fibre-product and representable-stack-morphism to specify the span groupoid.
The graph factorization over X identifies the joint map as a composite of the base change of p and a base change of the separated DM diagonal of Y; both are finite.
On scheme charts use native IsFinite and its base-change/composition instances.
acceptance: Retain distinct spans with the same image but different degree.
There is no obligation for the joint map to be a monomorphism.

nodes.title: Composition and change of base of finite correspondences
nodes.statement: Composition of finite correspondences by the two-fibre product has representable finite legs. It is associative up to the canonical associator equivalence, has identity spans as units, and commutes with arbitrary change of base. If all legs are finite locally free, the composite legs are finite locally free as well. These are stack-level statements; a coarse-space operation is not asserted to preserve the middle fibre product.

nodes.statement: For an fpqc cover S′→S, finite correspondences between the fixed endpoints X,Y over S form a groupoid equivalent to finite correspondences between X_{S′},Y_{S′} supplied with an isomorphism over S′×_S S′ satisfying the identity and triple-overlap cocycle, including the 2-isomorphisms on both legs. A descended span is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with the specified descent identification. Finite locally free legs descend too.

An actual fpqc descent datum is supplied on the middle stack and both legs, not merely matching geometric isomorphism classes.

nodes.title: Finite spans induce finite coarse spans
nodes.statement: A finite correspondence X←Z→Y as above induces M_X←M_Z→M_Y between the Keel–Mori coarse spaces, and both induced maps are finite. Formation of these maps commutes with flat change of the common base. Arbitrary base change is valid when each of X,Y,Z is tame. Neither preservation of degree nor preservation of middle fibre products follows in general.
hypotheses: X,Y are separated finite-type DM stacks over locally Noetherian S, with finite inertia.
The middle Z and both legs satisfy finite-correspondence; Z is then separated, finite type and has finite inertia.
The arbitrary-base assertion requires tameness of all three stacks.
proofSteps: Use SF.1/keel-mori for the three coarse spaces and categorical universality for the induced maps.

For the left induced map, π_X∘p= ar p∘π_Z is proper. After any base change, surjectivity of π_Z descends universal closedness to  ar p; separatedness and finite type come from the endpoint/coarse separation and local finite-type results.

After passage to an algebraically closed field, the classes in a coarse fibre are images of the finite fibre of p after choosing an isomorphism in X; this yields finitely many geometric points, hence quasi-finiteness for the finite-type coarse map.
Apply the algebraic-space theorem proper plus quasi-finite implies finite. Repeat for q; use coarse uniqueness for flat or tame base-change compatibility.

nodes.title: Finite flat descent through a tame coarse space
nodes.statement: Let π:X→M be the coarse space of a locally Noetherian tame algebraic stack with finite inertia. For a representable finite locally free p:Z→X, let A=p_*O_Z. If every stabilizer at a closed geometric point of X acts trivially on the fibre of A, then B=π_*A is a finite locally free commutative O_M-algebra, the adjunction π*B→A is an isomorphism of algebras, and Z≃X×_M Spec_M(B). The descended finite locally free morphism has the same rank. The condition is on the entire finite algebra, including its stabilizer action; a coarse geometric point bijection is insufficient.

p is representable finite locally free.
All closed geometric stabilizers act trivially on A fibres.

Apply Alper Theorem 10.3 to the vector bundle A.
Full faithfulness of pullback on vector bundles descends multiplication and unit; faithfulness verifies associativity, commutativity and the unit identities.

nodes.title: Normalization of a Deligne–Mumford stack
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally Noetherian DM stack. Choose an étale scheme atlas U→X, set R=U×_X U, and normalize U and R in the total rings of fractions of their reductions. Smooth normalization compatibility gives R^ν≅R×_U U^ν≅U^ν×_U R and the normalized étale groupoid. Its quotient X^ν has a representable integral map ν_X:X^ν→X, and for every smooth scheme chart V→X its pullback is the ordinary normalization V^ν. This characterizes the construction up to unique comparison isomorphism. On scheme charts use the imported SF.0 ordinary-normalization adapter to Mathlib’s relative normalization of the disjoint generic points; normalizing the identity map would be incorrect.
hypotheses: X is locally Noetherian and DM; more generally require the locally finite-component condition of Stacks Lemma 101.46.1.
Ordinary normalization removes nilpotents before integral closure.
proofSteps: Import ordinary scheme normalization and smooth base-change compatibility from SF.0 and the native qcqs relative-normalization API.
Lift source, target, inverse and composition on the normalized groupoid using the smooth comparisons; construct the unit from the base-changed identity section.
Verify groupoid axioms by normalization uniqueness and use SF.1/groupoid-space plus stack quotient.
Integral representability and chart characterization descend; compare two atlases on their common refinement.

Finiteness requires the additional Nagata condition below.
No arbitrary nonflat base-change theorem for ordinary normalization is included.

nodes.title: Schematic closure in a Deligne–Mumford stack
nodes.statement: For a quasi-compact morphism f:Z→X of locally Noetherian DM stacks, define its schematic image C⊂X to be the smallest closed substack through which f factors. For a smooth chart U→X the corresponding closed subscheme is cut out by ker(O_U→(f_U)_*O_{Z_U}); these ideal sheaves descend to X. For a quasi-compact immersion of an object over a dense open base this is its schematic closure. The construction retains scheme structure and commutes with flat base change. No nonflat comparison is asserted.
hypotheses: f is quasi-compact; X,Z are locally Noetherian DM stacks.
The closure use requires a specified immersion into the ambient stack.
proofSteps: Work on affine opens of smooth target charts. Quasi-compactness of f makes each pulled-back source quasi-compact; choose a finite union of quasi-compact étale scheme charts surjecting onto it. Use native Scheme.Hom.image and its kernel ideal sheaf for their quasi-compact composite to the target chart; faithfully flat source descent identifies its kernel with that of f.
Flat base change of the kernel identifies ideals on both projections of the atlas overlap. Descend the quasi-coherent ideal using SF.1 stack QCoh descent.
Minimality and factorization are local on the target; prove independence of charts.
For flat base change use the same kernel comparison.

nodes.title: When closure preserves finite correspondences
nodes.statement: Let S be integral locally Noetherian excellent, let U⊂S be dense open, and let X,Y be separated finite-type DM stacks over S with finite inertia. Suppose a finite correspondence C_U between X_U and Y_U has a quasi-compact joint immersion C_U→X_U×_U Y_U. Let C be its schematic closure in X×_S Y. If both projections C→X and C→Y are representable, proper and quasi-finite, then they are finite, so C is a finite correspondence extending C_U. Properness follows, for example, if both endpoint stacks are proper over S; quasi-finiteness is an additional condition. This procedure is for immersed spans and cannot replace finite-algebra extension for a general multiple-cover span.
hypotheses: All conditions in the statement, including the joint immersion and quasi-finiteness of both projections.
U is used rather than an unqualified generic fibre so that C_U embeds as the open-base restriction of C.
proofSteps: Construct the closure and restrict to U; an immersion already closed over U has its original schematic image there. The joint map of a finite span is finite, so the given immersion is closed over U.
If X,Y are proper over S, the product projections and closed-substack inclusions give properness of both legs.
Apply the requested algebraic-space proper quasi-finite finiteness theorem on each target chart; descend finiteness.
acceptance: For S=Spec(k[t]), the closure of the graph x=1/t from U=D(t) into X=S and Y=A1_S is Spec(k[t,1/t]); the projection to S is quasi-finite but not proper and is not finite.
A proper closure can have positive-dimensional special fibres; properness alone is insufficient.
The double-point span over a point cannot be extended by its one-point schematic image.

For normal C_U the normalized restriction is isomorphic to C_U.

review.notes: Independent target-level review of every node, all 29 pinned baseline statements, every cross-roadmap supplier contract, the current upstream ownership boundary, five definition/construction APIs and their tests, six planets and the honest Lean omission ledger. The read-only reader needs the corrections listed in the review report when packaged.

checked.note: Retained closed/flat/finitely-presented subgroup hypotheses and noncentral normality. Restricted the geometric bottom constructor to closed unit/separated inertia, added extensionality and a non-separated-group counterexample, and distinguished the unconditional site-level bottom.

AOV Appendix A pp.1087–1089 verifies quotient Isom sheaves followed by stackification. The identity-subgroup test now states its closedness hypothesis; global section cosets and nonsmooth bands remain discriminated.

Romagny Theorem 5.1(i), pp.224–225, plus AOV quotient Hom/stackification gives the Hom-groupoid equivalence for any stack target, including modifications and contractible factorization relative to a fixed comparison.
AOV Theorem A.1(b), p.1087: quotient epimorphism and kernel are assertions about fppf sheaves. The native categorical quotient is used only for the precursor congruence.

AOV Theorem A.1 and local BG proof, pp.1087–1089, give proper/étale map conditions. Clarified that Romagny 5.1(iii) descends properness of the stack rather than asserting properness of its rigidification map. General BG smoothness is explicitly requested.
Romagny Theorem 5.1, p.224, and the varying-subgroup quotient-sheaf construction give arbitrary base change; subgroup flatness/finite presentation is preserved.
A formal consequence of the Hom-groupoid universal property, with the residual G/H explicitly required closed, flat and finitely presented. No reversal for unrelated subgroups is claimed.
Romagny Theorem 5.1(iv) and the AOV gerbe model give the same all-algebraic-space universal property and geometric-point classes, without inferring fine moduli.

The closed flat finitely presented vertical kernel is killed by the universal factorization. Full test-scheme stabilizer injectivity, Stacks 101.6.2 (04YY), and the supplier setoid criterion prove representability; geometric injectivity alone is not used.

Read the predecessor affine-kernel-rigidification contract. The comparison needs its affine neutralization/descent plus the additional geometric subgroup hypotheses; representable final maps are not mistaken for full maps.

A representable level map takes preserving subgroups while rigidification takes quotients. Current ModularCurves 4C/9D supplies concrete rigidifiers; all-test-scheme trivial inertia is required for a space.

Both representable finite legs and the apex are retained. The separated DM diagonal gives joint finiteness. Added explicit span isomorphisms and their groupoid, needed by effective descent; the scheme prototype records both leg equations.

Two-fibre-product projections and composition preserve finite (or finite locally free) legs. Associators, units and base change follow from the pullback universal property; coarse middle pullbacks are not asserted preserved.

Flat base change, or tameness of all three stacks for arbitrary base change, is retained.

Full faithfulness descends the entire algebra, and the requested stack relative Spec imports its scheme owner AlgebraicVectorBundles. No general coherent-sheaf descent is claimed.
